text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: realtime-p99-latency breach for /v1/generate (EU region). p99 jumped to 4.2s, p95 ~1.1s. SLO breached. Auto-page sent to oncall.
oncall-jordan: I'm on it, joining bridge now. pinging infra and model teams. bridge: https://call.redwood/incident/4918273001
sre-alex: looking at host-level metrics — CPU ok, but GPU memory pressure and a spike in KV cache evictions for eu-* pools. Graph: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/latency?panel=99&from=now-10m
nico-ml: seeing increased kv_miss_rate on the LRU prefix cache for the rerank model serving EU. Miss rate went from 2% -> 18% in last 8m.
emily-prod: any customer-facing errors? Maya, can you check support queue for anything correlated with the timestamp?
maya-support: one customer ticket for slow responses (ACME Corp) filed 5m ago referencing timeouts in chat flow. No 5xxs logged, just long latencies. Ticket #3212.
oncall-jordan: quick mitigation ideas: 1) route EU traffic to global fallback pool (more capacity) 2) enable temporary lower-quality quantized model fallback 3) increase batch size/limits? What’s safest?
sre-alex: immediate safe is routing to fallback pool in another region with latency-tier routing. Will flip routing weight to fallback-2 for non-EU-restricted tenants. Running command now: ```./infra/route-tools set-weight --pool eu-main=60 --pool fallback-2=40 --note "latency spike 4918273001"```
infra-ops-bot: Routing change submitted by sre-alex, propagation started (approx 30s). New traffic weights: eu-main 60%, fallback-2 40%.
nico-ml: model note — fallback-2 uses a smaller model variant with slightly lower perplexity but much lower tail latency. Quality hit expected to be minor for short prompts.
emily-prod: post-change: check p95/p99 dashboards and sampling logs for customers moved. Also open a canary to ensure correctness on tool-calling paths.
oncall-jordan: checking logs — p99 dropped from 4.2s -> 1.8s after route change, p95 stable at ~0.9s. Still above target but trending down. Keeping channel open for 30m watch.
sre-alex: digging deeper on root cause: memory churn looks due to a recent config rollout that changed prefix-cache max_entries on eu pool (rolled 7m ago). Reverting that change for eu-main now: ```kubectl -n serving set env deployment/eu-runtime PREFIX_CACHE_MAX=40M --record``` — revert in flight.
nico-ml: if revert succeeds, kv miss rate should decline and tail will normalize. I'll monitor model-level metrics.
maya-support: notified impacted customer ACME via ticket with mitigation note and ETA 30m. No further escalations yet.
emily-prod: opening a follow-up postmortem stub and tagging rollout config change as suspected cause. We should mark as P1 until stabilization.
oncall-jordan: callout to oncall: if p99 stays >2s after 30m we'll escalate to full page and involve infra lead.
incident-bot: Incident timer started. Current incident state: mitigation-in-progress. Actions: routing rollback, config revert, customer notifications. Updates will be posted in thread.
sre-alex: revert completed, monitoring. kv_miss_rate dropping to 6% -> p99 trending to 1.1s. Will leave autoscaling alone for now.
nico-ml: baseline expected back within 10-15m. Will run a quick synthetic prompt sweep to confirm tail stability.
oncall-jordan: good work. Keep updates brief in this thread only. If anything changes dramatically ping #all-hands. :thumbsup:
